comparisons.peer_topic: Business Segment Structure and Reporting Basis
comparisons.peer_summary: Bank of America reports results through four business segments (Consumer Banking, GWIM, Global Banking, Global Markets) with remaining operations in All Other, managing and reporting on an FTE basis.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose their business segment structures and how residual or non-core operations are aggregated. Citi defines 'Legacy Franchises' within its 'All Other' managed basis to include winding-down operations and legacy assets like consumer mortgages. Similarly, Bank of America aggregates remaining operations not in its four main segments into 'All Other', reporting these results on a full-time equivalent (FTE) basis. While Citi explicitly lists specific legacy assets (Mexico Consumer, Asia Consumer exit, U.K. retail) in its All Other definition, BAC provides a broader structural definition of All Other without detailing specific legacy wind-downs in this segment summary, focusing instead on the management basis.

sentences.text: • Legacy Holdings Assets, primarily $2.0 billion of legacy consumer mortgage loans in North America, as well as the U.K. retail banking business, both of which Citi continues to wind down.
We report our results of operations through the following four business segments: Consumer Banking, GWIM, Global Banking and Global Markets, with the remaining operations recorded in All Other.
We manage our segments and report their results on an FTE basis.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Platform Solutions segment includes consumer platforms and transaction banking and other services.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures detail the composition of specific business segments. Citi’s target disclosure defines 'Legacy Franchises' (part of All Other) by listing specific geographic and asset components (Mexico, Asia exit, U.K. retail, $2.0B mortgages) that are being wound down. Goldman Sachs’ Platform Solutions segment includes 'consumer platforms' (like credit cards) and transaction banking. While Citi’s Legacy Franchises represent exiting or legacy holdings, GS’s Platform Solutions represents an active operating segment, but both disclosures use a similar method of breaking down complex segment definitions into constituent consumer-focused or legacy business lines.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Credit Portfolio Composition and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm's retained consumer portfolio primarily serves the prime segment and consists of residential real estate, credit card, scored auto, and business banking loans. Originated mortgages are typically securitized or sold, while other consumer loans are retained on the balance sheet.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the composition of consumer credit portfolios, specifically highlighting residential real estate loans. Citi includes '$2.0 billion of legacy consumer mortgage loans in North America' as part of its Legacy Holdings Assets within the All Other segment. JPMorgan describes its retained consumer portfolio which 'consists primarily of loans... for residential real estate'. Both banks explicitly mention residential real estate mortgages as a distinct component of their consumer-facing assets, though Citi characterizes them as legacy/winding down assets while JPM describes them as part of its active retained prime consumer portfolio.

sentences.text: • Legacy Holdings Assets, primarily $2.0 billion of legacy consumer mortgage loans in North America, as well as the U.K. retail banking business, both of which Citi continues to wind down.
The Firm's retained consumer portfolio consists primarily of loans and lending-related commitments for residential real estate, credit card, scored auto and business banking.
The consumer credit portfolio also includes loans at fair value, predominantly in residential real estate.

comparisons.peer_topic: Residential Real Estate Loan Types and Portfolio Status
comparisons.peer_summary: Residential real estate loans consist of first- and second-lien mortgages, including HELOCs, the vast majority of which are held for investment in the Wealth Management business segment's loan portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the nature and holding status of residential real estate loans. Citi identifies 'legacy consumer mortgage loans in North America' as a key component of its Legacy Holdings Assets, which it is winding down. Morgan Stanley defines its residential real estate loans as consisting of 'first- and second-lien mortgages, including HELOCs' and notes that the vast majority are 'held for investment' in its Wealth Management segment. Both filings isolate residential mortgages as a distinct asset class, with Citi focusing on the legacy/wind-down aspect and MS focusing on the investment holding and product type (first/second lien, HELOCs).
